title: Component coproduct over prescribed dense opens
statement: Let X be a reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and let ι_i:C_i→X, indexed by Fin(n), be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] from integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme] whose images enumerate without repetitions the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. For dense opens V_i⊆C_i, there is a dense open U⊆X such that the component coproduct morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] restricted to U is an isomorphism and ι_i^{-1}(U)⊆V_i for every i.

proof.text: Set Z_i = range(ι_i). Let W_i be the complement of the union of Z_j for j ≠ i. Finiteness makes it open. The generic point of Z_i lies in W_i: a containment Z_i ⊆ Z_j forces equality by maximality and then i=j by injectivity. The cover implies W_i ⊆ Z_i.

The restriction C_i ×_X W_i → W_i is a surjective closed immersion into a reduced scheme, hence an isomorphism: on affines the defining ideal lies in the nilradical and is zero. Intersect its source with V_i and transfer the intersection to an open O_i of X. The dense open V_i of integral C_i contains its generic point, so O_i contains the generic point of Z_i.

Take U = union of O_i. They are disjoint since W_i excludes every other component. The closure of U contains each component generic point and hence all components; it is X. Only O_i has a nonempty inverse image in C_i, and this inverse image lies in V_i. The maps C_i ×_X U → O_i are isomorphisms. Base change preserves finite scheme coproducts; their coproduct is Sigma.desc ι restricted to U and is an isomorphism. If n=0, the cover forces X empty and U is empty.
